facts.text: Time-history agreement compares an entire simulated curve over time with the corresponding physical-test curve to detect differences in timing and shape, not just peak values.
facts.quote: Time-history agreement compares a whole curve over time from the simulation with the same curve from the physical test, so that differences in timing and shape are caught, not only differences in the peak value.

facts.text: Time-history metrics score magnitude, phase and shape separately and then combine the scores.
facts.quote: Time-history metrics score magnitude (how big), phase (how early or late) and shape separately and then combine them.

facts.text: In the booklet's aviation seat comparison, simulated and measured peaks differed by only 0.3%, but the time-history error was 60.4%; a peak-only check would have classified the agreement as excellent.
facts.quote: In an aviation seat comparison, the simulated and measured peaks differed by only 0.3%, which a peak-only check would call excellent, yet the time-history error was 60.4%.

facts.text: In another comparison reported in the booklet, the peak error was 3.42% and the time-history error was 7.2%, both within the 10% guideline.
facts.quote: In another case the peak error was 3.42% and the time-history error 7.2%, both within the 10% guideline [Chapter 10].

facts.text: The Sprague-Geers error method used for the booklet's reported comparison figures combines a magnitude term and a phase term.
facts.quote: The method behind these figures is the Sprague-Geers error, which combines a magnitude term and a phase term.

facts.text: ISO 18571 is an international standard that combines corridor, phase, magnitude and slope scores into one rating of two time signals.
facts.quote: ISO 18571 is an international standard that rates two time signals with corridor, phase, magnitude and slope scores combined into one rating

facts.text: The booklet mentions ISO 18571 as the metric used in a 2026 demonstration correlating an automatic-braking controller with proving-ground tests.
facts.quote: the booklet mentions it as the metric in a 2026 demonstration correlating an automatic-braking controller with proving-ground tests

facts.text: Euro NCAP's virtual-testing protocol qualifies models using an "ISO score" and defined indicators.
facts.quote: Euro NCAP's virtual-testing protocol likewise qualifies models with an "ISO score" and defined indicators [Chapters 2, 3].

facts.text: CORA (correlation and analysis) is an older crash-safety rating method with a structure similar to ISO 18571; the passage identifies CORA as general background rather than a method mentioned in the booklet.
facts.quote: CORA (correlation and analysis) is an older crash-safety rating method with a similar structure; it is general background, not from the booklet.

facts.text: For automatic braking, the booklet recommends validating the whole causal timing chain rather than stopping distance alone: detection time, decision time, brake command time, pressure build-up, deceleration, speed and position histories, plus distance-to-object and relative-speed histories near the collision or no-collision boundary.
facts.quote: detection time, decision time, brake command time, pressure build-up, deceleration, speed and position histories, plus distance-to-object and relative-speed histories near the collision or no-collision boundary [Chapter 10].
